questions.stem: A technician is installing Windows on a brand-new computer that has no operating system yet. Which boot method is the most common today for getting the installer to run?

choices.text: A USB flash drive containing the installation files
An internal recovery partition that already exists on the new drive
Mapping a network share from another running Windows PC

questions.explanation: The transcript calls a bootable USB flash drive the most common boot method today for installing an OS on a system with no OS.
questions.trap: An internal recovery partition needs an OS already on the machine that created it; a brand-new computer with nothing installed will not have one populated.

questions.stem: A corporate IT team needs to install the same Windows image on 200 new desktops on the network as quickly as possible. Which boot method is designed for this scenario?

choices.text: USB boot, one machine at a time

questions.explanation: PXE / network boot is the corporate boot method specifically for installing an OS on many machines at once.
questions.trap: USB boot works, but doing 200 USBs one at a time is exactly the problem PXE was created to solve.

questions.stem: A user is moving from Windows 10 to Windows 11 and wants to keep their installed apps, settings, and personal files intact. Which installation type fits?
questions.explanation: An in-place upgrade installs the new OS while preserving existing files, applications, and settings.
questions.trap: A clean install wipes the partition. It is the safest install but loses everything not backed up.

questions.stem: A Windows installation has become corrupted, but the user's documents and profile are still intact. Which install type refreshes the OS files while leaving personal data untouched?

choices.text: In-place upgrade to the same version

questions.explanation: A repair installation refreshes the OS system files but leaves the user's personal data alone, which is exactly the corrupted-OS scenario described.
questions.trap: An in-place upgrade is meant for moving to a new version. The intent here is to repair the current one without changing version.

questions.stem: Which partition style is REQUIRED when installing Windows on a UEFI-based system?
questions.explanation: GPT is the modern partition style required for UEFI BIOS systems. It also supports up to 128 partitions and very large drive sizes.
questions.trap: MBR is the legacy style and cannot be used to boot a UEFI system. exFAT and ext4 are file systems, not partition styles.

questions.stem: Which two limits define the older MBR partition style?

choices.text: Maximum 128 partitions and roughly 16 TB drive size
Maximum 1 partition and 4 GB file size
Maximum 4 primary partitions and roughly 2 TB drive size
Maximum 4 partitions and 4 GB file size

questions.explanation: MBR is limited to 4 primary partitions and cannot address drives larger than about 2 TB.
questions.trap: The 4 GB number belongs to FAT32's file size limit, not to MBR's partition limits.

questions.stem: A drive that previously held confidential data is being repurposed and must have any residual data made unrecoverable as part of formatting. Which format type writes zeros across the entire disc?
questions.explanation: A full format is slow because it writes zeros across the entire disc, making the previous data far harder to recover. Quick format only rewrites the file system metadata.
questions.trap: Quick format is fine for a freshly bought drive but does not securely erase prior data.

questions.stem: Before upgrading a PC to Windows 11, the technician must verify two firmware-level features specifically required by Windows 11. Which two?

choices.text: MBR partitioning and BIOS legacy mode
TPM 2.0 and Secure Boot enabled in UEFI
DHCP and a static IP address
FAT32 system partition and APIPA enabled

questions.explanation: Windows 11 requires TPM 2.0 and Secure Boot, both enabled in the UEFI firmware, to install.
questions.trap: MBR plus legacy BIOS is actively the wrong direction; Windows 11 wants GPT plus UEFI plus TPM and Secure Boot.

questions.stem: A help-desk team needs to roll out one standardized, fully configured Windows build to hundreds of new PCs. Which deployment strategy fits?

choices.text: In-place upgrade from a USB stick

questions.explanation: Image deployment is the strategy of setting up one PC perfectly, capturing an image, and rapidly copying that image to many machines.
questions.trap: A per-device installation defeats the purpose; image deployment is specifically the efficient bulk option.

questions.stem: Windows releases two kinds of OS updates as part of the product life cycle. Which pairing matches each update type to its purpose?

choices.text: Both update types only add new features
Both update types only patch security holes
Quality updates add new features; feature updates patch security holes
Quality updates patch security and bug issues; feature updates add new functionality

questions.explanation: Quality updates are the regular small patches for security and reliability; feature updates are the larger periodic releases that add new functionality.
questions.trap: The reversed pairing - quality adds features, feature updates patch security - is the classic distractor; do not swap which one does which.
